sentences.text: Researchers conducted a forward-looking pilot study at a single hospital in Sweden over a three-year period to determine if specific blood proteins could distinguish brain injury from the effects of general anesthesia alone. The study measured blood samples from 21 stroke patients and 19 people undergoing non-brain surgery.

Scientists tested three specific proteins in blood drawn before the procedure and again two and twenty-four hours later, noting that GFAP levels did not rise in patients who only had non-brain surgery.

The authors suggest GFAP is a better marker because its levels did not rise in patients who only had non-brain surgery, though they state that more testing is needed to confirm GFAP as a reliable tool for detecting brain injury in hospital settings.
